subject: maths
question: A fruit dealer gets the cost price of 60 bananas by selling 40 bananas. What is the profit percent?
solution:
**Given:- **

(1) The cost price of 60 bananas = selling price of 40 bananas 

**Formula used:**- 

(1) Profit (P) = Selling Price (SP) - Cost Price (CP) 

(2) Profit % = ( Profit/CP) × 100 %

**Calculation:- **

Cost Price of 1 banana = 1/60 

Selling Price of 1 banana = 1/40 

So, Profit = (1/40) - (1/60)

Profit = ( 3 - 2)/120 

Profit = (1/120)

Then, Profit % = [(1/120)/(1/60)] × 100 

Profit % = (100/2)% 

Profit % = 50% 

**∴ The required answer is __ 50%__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

 

60 × CP = 40 × SP 

SP/CP = 60/40 

SP/CP = 3/2 

Profit % = [(3 - 2)/2] × 100 

**Profit % = 50% **
